chunks: And that which was narrated - Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Mis'mam, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to shave his head or shorten [his hair] until he became 'nafar' [shook off the minor state of Ihram], he said, 'He shaves in the way or wherever he is.'

So it is not contradictory to what we mentioned, because this narration is interpreted as applying to one who was unable to return to Mina. As for one who is able to do so, then it is necessary [to return], according to what we have previously stated. As for that which indicates that he should return his hair [shaving] to Mina if he shaved elsewhere, that is what was narrated:

key_terms.مَحْمُولَةٌ: interpreted/assigned (as applying to a specific case)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina (a sacred site near Mecca where Ihram rituals are completed)
key_terms.نَفَرَ: to shake off the minor state of Ihram (by shaving or shortening hair)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to shave their head in Mina?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in exiting Ihram when hair shaving is delayed, distinguishing between those unable to return to Mina and those who can. It underscores the Shia juristic principle that the location of shaving is not strictly bound to Mina unless the pilgrim has the capacity to return, thereby preventing undue hardship. This ruling reflects the broader Islamic legal ethos of ease (*taysir*) in ritual obligations.
